newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF's Camdessus pledges to back Romania reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus pledges to back Romania reforms.

text.p: International Monetary Fund head Michel Camdessus said on Saturday that Romania's new centrist government was pressing ahead with "courageous" reforms and pledged the Fund's full support.

Camdessus said he had only discussed general principles with President Emil Constantinescu's administration, which ousted ex-communists last month, ahead of talks next month on resuming suspended IMF credits.

He repeated the Fund's contention that the government had inherited a situation worse than previously thought from its leftist predecessor and praised its pledges to pursue reforms while remedying hardships of farmers, workers and families.

"I told the prime minister and his government that on the basis of these principles and the courageous action they want to undertake they will have the IMF's full support," Camdessus said after talks with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
"We will be by their side to explain to the rest of the world that what is happening now in Romania is important and deserves everyone's support."

The Fund suspended a $460 million three-year accord this year after criticising the previous administration's foreign exchange market restrictions and overspending ahead of the election that brought Constantinescu to power.
A week-long mission by Fund experts immediately after the election revealed grim economic indicators.

Year-on-year inflation of 47.4 percent in November was more than double the IMF-directed target of 20 percent for 1996, and the budget deficit surged to 5.7 percent of gross domestic product from initial pledges of 2.2 percent.

The government programme, approved by parliament, contains few figures but calls broadly for restraint in budget spending, liberalisation of foreign exchange markets and increased benefits for needy families.
Ciorbea told reporters IMF support would help put the programme on the rails and attract foreign investment.
"The new government is determined to keep to the provisions of a new (IMF) memorandum and allay any doubts or hesitation in trusting Romania's cabinet or its people," he said.
"We have to be open and straightforward with both the Fund and our own people. We have to explain all the aspects of measures to be taken, including the painful effects."
Camdessus, the IMF's Managing Director, was meeting opposition leaders and trade unions before a news conference to close out his 24-hour visit.

As he arrived, Ciorbea announced increases in fuel prices in line with IMF recommendations. The Fund has also sought budget cuts, a postponement in raising child benefits, higher discount rates and reduced central bank funds to farmers.
